title: POC scoping - burst patterns & token-mix profiling (VeloxHealth)
next_steps: SE to run synthetic QPS/latency baseline on Redwood sandbox by 2025-02-26
AE to share sizing spreadsheet and pricing tiers
Customer to provide 3 representative traffic traces and sample prompt set
action_items: Priya Nair: run 3 synthetic profiles (steady qps, bursty qps, long-sequence) and share results by 2025-02-26
Jordan Kim: send pricing + dedicated vs hosted comparison doc by 2025-02-21
Aisha Rahman: upload traffic traces (gzip) and top-200 prompts to shared drive by 2025-02-24
summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on characterizing VeloxHealth's bursty query patterns, concurrency targets, and token distribution for a triage/chat use case. Main goals: define success criteria (latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens, quality regression tolerance), determine workload sizing for Dedicated vs Hosted, and plan benchmarks. SE will run synthetic profiles; customer will provide real traces. Security & compliance (SAML, SOC2) noted as gating for Dedicated/private deployment.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm jordan from redwood, i'm the AE on this one. quick quick intros?
[00:08] Aisha Rahman: sure, i'm aisha, head of ml at veloxhealth, we run the triage agent and a small clinical faq bot.
[00:14] Tom Aguilar: tom, platform eng, i manage infra and api gateway.
[00:18] Mei Chen: mei, security lead. I'll listen for compliance items.
[00:22] Priya Nair: hi all, priya here, i'll be your SE. excited to dig into traffic patterns.
[00:27] Jordan Kim: perfect. goal for today: scope a poc to validate costs and latency under your real workload and some synthetic bursts. we want to agree success criteria, datasets, and timeline.
[00:36] Aisha Rahman: high level: our triage product gets variable traffic—mostly steady during day but very spiky when API is called from partners after announcements. typical baseline is 12 qps with bursts to 600 qps for 30-120 seconds. we also have a smaller conversational flow with long contexts occasionally.
[00:52] Priya Nair: helpful. can you confirm average input token lengths and output lengths? like median, p90?
[00:58] Aisha Rahman: median input about 45 tokens, p90 220, outputs median 60 tokens, p90 450. but for the long context flows we see sequences up to 3k tokens end-to-end.
[01:10] Tom Aguilar: also, about concurrency—we currently do per-request sync inference, upstream connection timeout is 30s, so latency SLO ideally < 700ms for 95, but we can tolerate up to 1.5s occasionally.
[01:22] Priya Nair: okay, so target 95th latency < 700ms and absolute SLA for pilot < 1.5s. that helps. are you using any caching/prefix reuse today?
[01:30] Aisha Rahman: minimal. we tried simple prompt caching for templated questions but prefix caching for chat is not in use.
[01:36] Jordan Kim: for the POC we usually test three profiles: (1) steady-state qps, (2) short burst profile matching your 600 qps spikes, (3) long-sequence throughput. we simulate client behavior and measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, and cost per 100k tokens.
[01:50] Mei Chen: security—if we go Dedicated or Private later we will need SAML SSO, KMS integration, and SOC2 audit evidence. is that covered?
[01:58] Jordan Kim: yes, redwood has SOC2 + SAML integrations; priya can share the security pack and compliance sheet. private deploy supports customer-managed KMS/HSM.
[02:06] Priya Nair: i'll share the security docs in the follow-up. also note, for bursts we often recommend autoscaling policies tuned to queue depth and a warm standby pool to avoid cold-starts on GPUs.
[02:16] Tom Aguilar: question—how do you model burst cost? if we provision dedicated GPUs for a 1% occurrence of bursts that's expensive. alternate is host and fall back.
[02:25] Jordan Kim: right—there are two levers: Dedicated reserved capacity sized for baseline + some buffer, and then capacity pool for burst that either spins up or routes to Hosted fallback to control cost. we can show cost modeling.
[02:36] Priya Nair: for sizing we'll need three numbers from your traces: qps time-series (1s granularity preferred), token-length distribution per request, and concurrency histogram (how many simultaneous open requests).
[02:45] Aisha Rahman: we can export 72 hours of logs, will that be enough?
[02:48] Priya Nair: yes, 48-72 hours is ideal. gzip and share link. also please anonymize PHI; we only need token counts and latencies.
[02:56] Aisha Rahman: understood.
[02:58] Tom Aguilar: on benchmarks, what's your default model selection? we want a 7B-ish open model for the POC, but with quantization. is that supported?
[03:06] Priya Nair: yes we have multiple verified 7B-13B models and quantization profiles. for latency/throughput baselines we usually test an FP16 and an 8-bit quantized run to show the delta.
[03:15] Jordan Kim: we'll report tokens/sec and cost-per-token across model variants. also measure quality delta—Aisha, do you have evaluation prompts to compute a simple pass/fail metric for generation?
[03:24] Aisha Rahman: yes, we have a scored prompt set for triage classification and a handful of safety/regulatory checks. p80 quality threshold is key; if quality drop > 3% we consider it failure.
[03:34] Priya Nair: good, we'll run both perf and quality. for perf we'll run: 1) steady 12 qps for 30 min; 2) synthetic burst: ramp 12 -> 600 qps over 10s hold for 60-120s then ramp down; 3) long-context: 3k token sequences at 2-4 qps.
[03:50] Tom Aguilar: for the burst test do you keep concurrency capped per GPU and use more nodes or queue? how do you avoid building huge queues?
[03:57] Priya Nair: we model both approaches: scale horizontally (more inference workers) and queueing with prioritization. we'll capture queue latency and dropped requests. in production we recommend autoscale with short queue allowances and a fast fallback to hosted endpoints if queue depth exceeds threshold.
[04:12] Jordan Kim: question to the group—what's the acceptance criteria for the POC? Aisha?
[04:18] Aisha Rahman: acceptance: (1) 95th latency <=700ms for baseline steady-state, (2) during a 600 qps burst we want 95th <=1.2s for at least 90% of burst time and no more than 0.5% errors, (3) quality regression <=3% vs our baseline model, (4) cost modelling shows < $X per 1M tokens for a mixed profile (we'll define X with Jordan).
[04:40] Jordan Kim: good—sounds measurable. we'll map these to the benchmark runs.
[04:44] Mei Chen: can we also include an audit of logs/retention and how KV cache is handled for privacy? we need clear data residency statements.
[04:52] Priya Nair: absolutely; the POC will include a short security checklist: data flow diagram, retention settings, KMS key ownership, and logs export sample.
[04:59] Tom Aguilar: timeframe—how long to run the POC?
[05:02] Jordan Kim: typical POC is 2-3 weeks: week 1 ingest traces and spin up sandbox, week 2 run perf/quality benchmarks and iterate, week 3 finalize recommendations and cost model. we can compress to two weeks if customer can provide traces and eval prompts quickly.
[05:16] Aisha Rahman: we can do a compressed timeline—aim for 2 weeks.
[05:19] Priya Nair: ok, so timeline: deliver synthetic baseline results by 2/26, then run customer-supplied traces/benchmarks 2/27-3/3, final report by 3/6.
[05:29] Jordan Kim: adding pricing follow-up by 2/21. we'll also propose Dedicated sizing vs Host+burst fallback.
[05:36] Aisha Rahman: for the synthetic tests, please simulate client retry behavior—we tend to have exponential backoff that doubles requests in bad windows.
[05:43] Priya Nair: noted, we'll include a retry pattern variant that mimics 2x retry with jitter.
[05:47] Tom Aguilar: what telemetry will you provide? we need token-level breakdown and per-route costs.
[05:52] Priya Nair: we'll provide a CSV of per-run metrics (timestamp, qps, concurrency, p50/p95/p99, token_throughput, infra_cost_usd), plus a dashboard link for deeper drill-down.
[06:03] Mei Chen: for SAML and KMS can you provide the required role mappings and key rotation policy?
[06:09] Jordan Kim: yes i'll include the admin guide and role mapping examples; KMS rotation policies are in the security pack.
[06:16] Aisha Rahman: are there any known gotchas with long-sequence contexts and kv cache eviction we should watch for?
[06:22] Priya Nair: long contexts increase KV cache memory and can push memory limits—we'll track cache hit ratios and memory per-worker. if you have repeated prefixes we can enable prefix caching to reduce recompute.
[06:32] Aisha Rahman: okay makes sense.
[06:35] Jordan Kim: ok last thing—artifacts to exchange: 1) Velox to share 72h trace + top-200 prompts + quality rubric; 2) Redwood will share security pack, pricing tiers, synthetic benchmark script and results, and dedicated sizing recommendation. Links will be posted in the follow-up thread.
[06:53] Aisha Rahman: one more question—if pilot goes well, what's typical migration path to private? timelines?
[06:58] Jordan Kim: private takes longer—about 6-10 weeks including infra provisioning and tests; Dedicated can be live in 2-4 weeks after contract. we'll include that in the write-up.
[07:08] Tom Aguilar: ok, thanks.
[07:10] Jordan Kim: cool. wrap up—recap next steps (pri... priya runs synthetic profiles, jordan sends pricing and docs, aisha uploads traces). any objections?
[07:20] Aisha Rahman: none. thanks all.
[07:23] Mei Chen: thanks.
[07:24] Priya Nair: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[07:26] Jordan Kim: end.
